Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the left hemithorax with ipsilateral mediastinal shift (trachea and heart shifted to the left), which is characteristic of volume loss due to lung collapse. The CT scan confirms a large central mass obstructing the left main bronchus, leading to left lower lobe (and likely total left lung) collapse, distinguishing it from a pleural effusion which would cause contralateral shift.
